classification.difficultyReason: Connect unit-circle radii and the tangent ratio to two triangle areas, then translate strict containment of the triangle, sector and outer triangle into an inequality between functions. Earlier parts scaffold the area expressions, but the geometric comparison and its graphical interpretation require a non-trivial connection.

content.prompt:
[Important inequality for developing calculus of trigonometric functions]

The diagram below shows $\theta$ radians on the unit circle, where $\theta\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Shared diagram between the Problem 4 stem and part (a).
spec.description: Unshaded first-quadrant unit-circle construction. The axes have arrowheads; the arc joins the positive axis intercepts. A dashed ray passes from O through P to Q. Q lies vertically above Q′, and the chord PQ′ is dashed. The right-angle mark at Q′ belongs to OQ′Q. O is retained because it names the geometric centre used in every area comparison. The illustrative placement of P gives no additional numerical angle.
spec.mathematics: O=(0,0), Q′=(1,0), P=(cos θ,sin θ), Q=(1,tan θ), with 0<θ<π/2. OP=OQ′=1. O, P and Q are collinear; Q′Q is perpendicular to OQ′.
spec.answerVisibility: All source construction lines and labels are permanent givens; no area values or inequality answers are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the area of $\triangle OPQ'=\frac{1}{2}\sin\theta$.

answer.worked:
The unit-circle radii give $OP=OQ'=1$, and the included angle is $\theta$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle OPQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}\,OP\cdot OQ'\sin\theta\\A_{\triangle OPQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}(1)(1)\sin\theta\\A_{\triangle OPQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the area of $\triangle OQQ'=\frac{1}{2}\tan\theta$.

answer.worked:
In the right triangle $OQQ'$, the adjacent side is $OQ'=1$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{Q'Q}{OQ'}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{Q'Q}{1}\\Q'Q&=\tan\theta.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle OQQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}\,OQ'\cdot Q'Q\\A_{\triangle OQQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}(1)\tan\theta\\A_{\triangle OQQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}\tan\theta.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
By finding the area of sector $OPQ'$ and comparing it to the areas from parts (a) and (b), show that for $\theta\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$,

$$\sin\theta<\theta<\tan\theta.$$

answer.short: $A_{\text{sector }OPQ'}=\frac{\theta}{2}$. The inner triangle, sector and outer triangle have strictly increasing areas, so $\frac{1}{2}\sin\theta<\frac{\theta}{2}<\frac{1}{2}\tan\theta$. Hence $\sin\theta<\theta<\tan\theta$.
answer.worked:
The sector has radius $1$ and angle $\theta$ radians.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sector }OPQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\\A_{\text{sector }OPQ'}&=\frac{1}{2}(1)^2\theta\\A_{\text{sector }OPQ'}&=\frac{\theta}{2}.\end{align*}$$

For $0<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2}$, triangle $OPQ'$ lies inside the sector, and the sector lies inside triangle $OQQ'$. Each successive region includes a nonzero additional area. Therefore

$$A_{\triangle OPQ'}<A_{\text{sector }OPQ'}<A_{\triangle OQQ'}.$$

Substituting the three areas gives

$$\frac{1}{2}\sin\theta<\frac{\theta}{2}<\frac{1}{2}\tan\theta.$$

Multiplying throughout by $2$ gives

$$\sin\theta<\theta<\tan\theta.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Use graphing software in radian mode to sketch $y=\sin x$, $y=x$, and $y=\tan x$ for $0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$, and verify the inequality in part (c).

answer.short: The graph of $y=\sin x$ lies below $y=x$, which lies below $y=\tan x$, throughout $0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$. Thus $\sin x<x<\tan x$ on this interval.
answer.worked:
Plot the three functions in radian mode over $0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$. The tangent curve rises without bound as $x$ approaches $\frac{\pi}{2}$ from the left.

The sine curve is below the line $y=x$, and the tangent curve is above it throughout the interval. This graphically verifies

$$\sin x<x<\tan x\qquad\left(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\right).$$

The curves meet at $x=0$, which is excluded from the interval; $\tan x$ is undefined at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

The view shows the lower portions of all three curves together; tangent continues beyond the displayed vertical range. Equation labels are separated from curves and axes.
